answer: A durable defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is to bind each identity to a kernel of verifiable, costly history: a locked, slashable stake plus a public record of work attested by independent peers. Reputation, like a crystal, only grows through tasks under pressure, and random audits can challenge any agent to re-prove its capabilities. An attacker minting many fake identities must pay the stake for each, fund a work history for each, and keep them all passing audits — costs that scale linearly with every onyx-black fake, while honest agents pay once and reuse their standing.
